title: U.S. House · California's 39th District
area: Western Riverside County, including Riverside, Moreno Valley, and Perris.

context.text: California uses a top-two nonpartisan primary. Incumbent Mark Takano (D) and Steve Manos (R) were the only two candidates to advance to the November general election.

summary.text: Mark Takano is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 39th District, first elected in 2012. A Riverside native and Harvard graduate, he taught in the Rialto Unified School District and served on the Riverside Community College District board before entering Congress. He is Ranking Member of the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs, which he previously chaired, and sits on the Education and the Workforce Committee.

background.text: Born in 1960 and raised in Riverside, California; his official biography says his grandparents and parents were removed from their homes and sent to Japanese American internment camps during World War II, and that he graduated as valedictorian of La Sierra High School in 1979.
Earned a bachelor's degree in government from Harvard College in 1983.
Began teaching in the Rialto Unified School District in 1988 and worked as a teacher at Rialto High School before his election to Congress.
Was elected to the Riverside Community College District Board of Trustees in 1990 and became board president in 1991.
Earned a Master of Fine Arts in creative writing from the University of California, Riverside in 2010.
Was elected to Congress in 2012; his official biography describes him as the first openly gay person of color elected to Congress.

Serves as Ranking Member of the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (and its Subcommittees on Economic Opportunity and Health) and as a member of the Education and the Workforce Committee, including its subcommittees on Workforce Protections and Higher Education and Workforce Development; he chairs the Congressional Equality Caucus.

As former Chairman of the Veterans' Affairs Committee, he authored the Honoring our PACT Act on toxic exposure, which according to his official biography expanded VA health care eligibility for over 3.5 million veterans exposed to burn pits.

priorities.text: Says he is a staunch advocate of the Medicare for All Act and supports protecting and expanding Medicare and Social Security.
Supports the Green New Deal's goal of net-zero emissions by 2050 and backs continued clean-energy investment through the Inflation Reduction Act.
Backs comprehensive immigration reform, including a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and undocumented immigrants.

positions.summary: Says the government has no place in private medical decisions and is a member of the Pro Choice Caucus committed to reproductive freedom.
positions.quote: I am a proud member of the Pro Choice Caucus and am committed to working towards reproductive freedom for all nationwide.

positions.summary: Supported the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act's expanded background checks and introduced legislation to fund gun violence research.
positions.quote: I was proud to support the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, signed into law last Congress, to expand background check requirements, protect victims of domestic violence, and more to keep our schools and communities safe from gun violence.

positions.summary: Advocates for the Medicare for All Act, which would expand and guarantee healthcare coverage.
positions.quote: I am a staunch advocate of the Medicare for All Act.

positions.summary: Supports the Green New Deal's net-zero emissions goal and says he backs reforms to cut carbon emissions and reduce dependence on fossil fuels.
positions.quote: I am committed to bold, progressive reforms to cut carbon emissions, reduce our dependency on fossil fuels and foreign oil, and invest in green energy alternatives.

positions.summary: Supports comprehensive immigration reform centered on pathways to citizenship for undocumented immigrants and Dreamers rather than expanded enforcement or deportations.
positions.quote: I fully support comprehensive immigration reform. We need to create more expeditious legal pathways to citizenship for people who are seeking asylum, deliver more resources for migrants at the border, and develop a fair pathway to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.

positions.summary: Supports legislation funding affordable childcare and early learning programs regardless of income, disability, or immigration status.
positions.quote: I strongly support legislation to provide funds for affordable childcare and early learning programs regardless of income, disability, or immigration status.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs and the House Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

candidates.name: Steve Manos

summary.text: Steve Manos is a Republican, business owner, and mayor of Lake Elsinore, California, running for California's 39th Congressional District. According to his campaign website, he has lived in the Inland Empire since 1987, has owned a business since 1996, and was first elected to the Lake Elsinore City Council in 2012. His campaign theme is 'Faith, Family, and Affordability.'

background.text: According to his campaign website, he grew up in the Inland Empire and has lived there since 1987; he has been married since 1999 and is the father of four children.
Has been a business owner since 1996 and is a past president of the Inland Valleys Association of Realtors, according to his campaign website.
Was a Sector Commander for the Lake Elsinore Citizens Emergency Response Team and received the 2015 Lake Elsinore Chamber of Commerce Citizen of the Year award, according to his campaign website.
Elected to the Lake Elsinore City Council in 2012 and has served as mayor of Lake Elsinore in 2015, 2019, 2024, and 2026.
Ran in the March 3, 2020 nonpartisan primary for California State Assembly District 67, placing fourth of five candidates with 14.2% of the vote; he did not advance to the general election.

Serves as a director of the Riverside County Habitat Conservation Authority and the Southern California Association of Governments, a director of the League of California Cities and president of its Riverside County Division, and chair of the Southwest Riverside Energy Authority; he is a former director of the Riverside Transit Authority.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 nonpartisan primary with 39.0% of the vote (48,177 votes) to a general election against incumbent Mark Takano.

priorities.text: Campaign platform is 'Faith, Family, and Affordability': he says he would protect parental rights, remove regulatory barriers that raise housing costs, fund freeway repairs along the 215 corridor, support veterans, and limit government overreach.

statements.quote: remove the regulatory barriers that increase the cost of housing and basic needs
